checks.label: World-Writable Device Nodes (Non-Standard)
checks.description: Lists character device nodes writable by any process, excluding the set Android makes world-writable by design (null, zero, urandom, tty, ptmx, the binder family, ashmem, ion, the primary GPU node and the sound nodes). Every remaining entry is an ioctl surface reachable from an unprivileged app or from an untrusted native process, and vendor driver ioctls are where a large share of Android kernel privilege escalations live. Reported as an inventory rather than pass or fail because the legitimate set is SoC-specific: a Qualcomm device exposes different nodes from a MediaTek or Exynos one, and failing on any entry would fire on every device.
checks.remediation: For each node listed, confirm the SELinux policy restricts it to the domains that need it and that the DAC permissions are not broader than the policy. Remove world write access from any node no app needs to reach directly.

checks.label: DSP / FastRPC Node Exposure
checks.command:
N=$(ls -d /dev/adsprpc-smd /dev/cdsprpc-smd /dev/fastrpc-adsp /dev/fastrpc-cdsp /dev/fastrpc* 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr '
' ' '); if [ -z "$N" ]; then echo NO_FASTRPC_NODE; else P=$(ls -l $N 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1" "$NF}' | tr '
' ' '); W=$(find /dev -maxdepth 1 -type c -perm -o+w -name '*rpc*' 2>/dev/null | tr '
' ' '); echo "FASTRPC_PRESENT perms=$P world_writable=${W:-none}"; fi
checks.description: Reports whether the Qualcomm FastRPC remote-procedure nodes to the ADSP and CDSP are present and how they are permissioned. CVE-2024-43047 is a use-after-free in this driver that appeared on the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list, and it was reachable because the node is accessible to applications by design on Qualcomm hardware. The existing CVE-033 check evaluates only the security patch date; this reports the attack surface itself, so an auditor can see whether the driver is actually reachable on the device in front of them rather than inferring it from a date. Presence is normal on Qualcomm SoCs and is not a finding on its own.
checks.remediation: Confirm the security patch level covers CVE-2024-43047 (see CVE-033) and that SELinux confines the fastrpc nodes to the domains that legitimately use the DSP. On a device with no DSP workload, remove app access to the node entirely.

checks.label: DMA-BUF Heaps and Legacy ION Exposure
checks.command: H=$(ls /dev/dma_heap/ 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); I=$([ -e /dev/ion ] && ls -l /dev/ion 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'); echo "dma_heap=${H:-none} legacy_ion=${I:-absent}"
checks.description: Reports the DMA-BUF heaps exposed under /dev/dma_heap and whether the legacy /dev/ion node is still present. Both provide shared buffers between userspace, the GPU, the camera and the DSP, so a bug in a heap exporter or in the importing driver is reachable from an app that can open the node. The legacy ION allocator was removed from mainline in favour of DMA-BUF heaps and its continued presence indicates an older vendor kernel. Informational: the exposed heap set is SoC-specific and having heaps is normal.
checks.remediation: Prefer DMA-BUF heaps over legacy ION when the kernel supports both, and confirm SELinux restricts each heap to the domains that need it. A device still exposing /dev/ion is running a kernel old enough to be worth checking against the ION CVE history.

checks.label: GPU Device Node Permissions
checks.command: N=$(ls -d /dev/kgsl-3d0 /dev/mali0 /dev/dri/card0 /dev/dri/renderD128 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); if [ -z "$N" ]; then echo NO_GPU_NODE; else ls -l $N 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1" "$3":"$4" "$NF}'; fi
checks.description: Reports the ownership and permissions of the GPU device nodes. The GPU driver is one of the largest ioctl surfaces reachable from an unprivileged app, because every app that renders must be able to open it, and it has a long CVE history across Adreno (kgsl), Mali and the DRM render nodes. App access is required for normal operation, so this is an inventory for review rather than a pass or fail; what matters is that the node is confined by SELinux and that the kernel carries current patches.
checks.remediation: Confirm the GPU driver is current against the SoC vendor advisories, and that SELinux confines the node to app and system domains rather than leaving it globally reachable.

checks.label: Binder Device Node Permissions
checks.command: N=$(ls -d /dev/binder /dev/hwbinder /dev/vndbinder /dev/binderfs/* 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); if [ -z "$N" ]; then echo NO_BINDER_NODE; else ls -l $N 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF" "$1}' | tr '\n' ' '; echo; fi
checks.description: Reports the permissions of the binder, hwbinder and vndbinder nodes. Binder is the transport for essentially every privileged operation on Android, and the driver itself has produced several exploited use-after-free vulnerabilities including CVE-2019-2215 and CVE-2023-20938. The nodes are world-accessible by design because every app needs binder, so the permissions are expected to be broad; this check records them so an auditor can confirm they match the platform default rather than having been widened, and so a device using binderfs is visible.
checks.remediation: Nothing to change under normal conditions. Confirm the permissions match the stock image for this build, and that the kernel carries the binder CVE fixes tracked in the CVE_INDICATORS category.

checks.label: Radio Diagnostic Interface Exposure
checks.command: N=$(ls -d /dev/diag /dev/diag_router /dev/smd0 /dev/smd11 /dev/smdcntl0 /dev/at_usb0 /dev/ttyGS0 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); if [ -z "$N" ]; then echo NO_DIAG_NODE; else W=$(find /dev -maxdepth 1 \( -name 'diag*' -o -name 'smd*' -o -name 'at_*' -o -name 'ttyGS*' \) -perm -o+rw 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); [ -n "$W" ] && echo "DIAG_WORLD_ACCESSIBLE $W" || echo "DIAG_PRESENT_RESTRICTED $N"; fi
checks.description: Detects the Qualcomm DIAG, shared-memory and AT command interfaces and whether they are readable and writable by any process. The DIAG interface speaks directly to the modem and exposes memory peek and poke, NV item read and write, and logging of every call and message. When /dev/diag is world-accessible a local app reaches the baseband without any permission, and when it is exposed over USB it is reachable with physical access alone. NO_DIAG_NODE is treated as passing: most production builds remove these nodes and their absence is the correct state.
checks.remediation: Remove the DIAG and AT nodes from production builds. Where a node must exist for manufacturing, restrict it to root with SELinux confinement and ensure it is not enumerated over USB in the shipping USB configuration.
checks.why: DIAG gives direct modem access including memory read and write and NV item manipulation, with no Android permission involved.
checks.risk_if_fail: A local app or anyone with physical USB access can read and alter modem state, intercept traffic and extract identifiers.

checks.label: Thermal Control Interface Permissions
checks.command: W=$(find /sys/class/thermal /sys/devices/virtual/thermal -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -o+w | head -10); [ -z "$W" ] && echo NO_WORLD_WRITABLE_THERMAL || printf '%s\n' "$W"
checks.description: Lists thermal zone and cooling device sysfs files writable by any process. Writable trip points and cooling device states let an unprivileged process disable throttling, which on a fanless POS terminal, kiosk or embedded device is a route to sustained overheating, thermal shutdown or hardware damage, and on a phone is a battery and performance denial of service. Reported as an inventory rather than pass or fail because some platforms legitimately expose specific cooling controls to a privileged system group and the layout is entirely SoC-specific.
checks.remediation: Restrict thermal sysfs writes to the system or thermal service UID and confirm SELinux labels the nodes so only the thermal HAL may write them.
